books.title: Everyday English
books.subtitle: Small conversations, big connections
books.description: Build confidence in the conversations that happen every day, from introductions to ordering a coffee.

resources.title: A new beginning
resources.transcript: Hello! Welcome to your English class. My name is Alex. I am curious about the world, and I love learning new things. Today, we will start a new journey together. Listen carefully, ask questions, and be kind to your classmates. A little practice every day makes a big difference. Let us begin.

resources.title: Start with hello
resources.transcript:
Hello. A new conversation starts here.
How are you today?
I am well. Thank you for asking.

lessons.title: The art of small talk
lessons.description: Turn a simple hello into a real conversation.

sections.title: Start with something you share
sections.body: Small talk helps people feel comfortable. Start with the place you are in, the weather, or an activity you share. Try saying 'This is a lovely classroom' or 'How was your weekend?'

sections.title: Keep the conversation going
sections.body: Ask an open question. Instead of 'Do you like books?', try 'What kind of books do you enjoy?' Listen to the answer and ask one more question. Share a little about yourself too.

sections.title: Try it with a partner
sections.body: Say hello to a classmate. Ask about their favourite food, a place they want to visit, or something they did yesterday. Spend two minutes listening before you switch roles.

lessons.question: Which question is most likely to start a longer conversation?
options: What do you enjoy doing after class?
lessons.explanation: An open question invites the other person to share more than a yes or no answer.

lessons.title: Everyday habits, simple sentences
lessons.description: Talk about the things you do, day after day.

sections.title: Meet the present simple
sections.body: Use the present simple for habits and facts. 'I walk to school.' 'They study English.' With he, she, and it, add -s or -es. 'She reads every morning.' 'He watches films.'

sections.title: Questions and negatives
sections.body: Use do or does to ask a question. 'Do you like music?' 'Does she play tennis?' Use do not or does not for a negative. 'I do not drink coffee.' After does, use the base verb without -s.

lessons.question: Choose the correct sentence.
lessons.explanation: With she, add -s to the verb in the present simple.

lessons.title: Ask a little more
lessons.description: Use who, what, and where in everyday questions.

sections.title: Choose a question word
sections.body: Use who for a person, what for a thing, and where for a place. 'Who is your teacher?' 'What is in your backpack?' 'Where is the classroom?'

sections.title: Keep the question in order
sections.body: With be, put the verb before the subject. 'Where is the kitchen?' With other present-simple verbs, use do or does. 'What do you read?' Ask a partner three questions and listen to each answer.

lessons.question: Choose the question that asks about a place.
lessons.explanation: Where asks about a place, and a garden is a place.

lessons.title: Ordering a meal
lessons.description: Ask for food and drinks politely.

sections.title: Make a simple request
sections.body: Say 'I would like' when ordering. 'I would like some bread, please.' Use 'Can I have' for a friendly request. 'Can I have some water, please?'

sections.title: Check and finish
sections.body: Ask 'How much is it?' when you need the price. Say 'Thank you' when the food arrives. Practise with a partner. One person is hungry and orders breakfast. The other takes the order. Then switch.

lessons.question: Which request sounds polite?
options: Can I have some water, please?
lessons.explanation: Can I have and please make this a polite request.
